# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary — 2026-07-24

US exchanges command the liquidity hierarchy, with Nasdaq 100 and NYSE delivering exceptional execution quality: Nasdaq's 0.0024% ILLIQ per $1M traded and 0.7711% AR spread are offset by dominant comparable volume of $295.7M, while NYSE's tighter 0.6278% spread but higher 0.0057% ILLIQ reflects its larger cap-weighted constituents. The Asian tier—Tokyo, Hong Kong, and Korea—shows divergent profiles: TSE ranks third with 2.4565% turnover despite 0.0361% ILLIQ, while Korea Exchange lags sharply at 1.6143% AR spread and 0.1463% ILLIQ despite 0.6994% turnover, signaling execution difficulty despite nominal activity. European venues split cleanly into mid-pack (Euronext at 0.0302% ILLIQ and $9.9M volume) and laggards (SIX Swiss at 0.0444% ILLIQ but only $3.3M volume, and LSE at 0.0812% ILLIQ with the worst 0.7973% spread). Xetra presents an intriguing compression: its 0.6699% AR spread ranks competitively mid-table, yet 0.0525% ILLIQ places it eighth, suggesting microstructure efficiency masks underlying depth constraints. For cross-border execution, liquidity fragmentations across currency zones demand careful venue selection below $10M notional.
